prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: I have passed the competitive examination (A) / three years ago, but I have not received (B) / any official appointment letter yet. (C) / No Error (D)
options: I have passed the competitive examination (A)
three years ago, but I have not received (B)
explanation: The present perfect cannot be used with a definite past time marker like 'three years ago'; 'I have passed' should be 'I passed'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The senior administrative officer (A) / had left the office premises (B) / an hour ago to attend a sudden inspection. (C) / No Error (D)
explanation: A definite past time expression such as 'an hour ago' requires the simple past, so 'had left' should be 'left'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The historic treaty is signed (A) / by the representatives of both nations (B) / in Paris on the tenth of October, 1999. (C) / No Error (D)
explanation: The completed past event dated 1999 requires the past passive: 'is signed' should be 'was signed'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: I have seen him yesterday (A) / at the crossroad traffic junction but he (B) / did not notice my vehicle passing by. (C) / No Error (D)
options: at the crossroad traffic junction but he
did not notice my vehicle passing by.
explanation: The present perfect cannot be used with a definite past time like 'yesterday'; part (A) should be the simple past, 'I saw him yesterday'.
